adjudication_records.issue_text: updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) in CalendarService.ts:1022 passes an empty update payload which Prisma rejects and cannot bump updatedAt, breaking cache refresh logic
deleteCache mutation in CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx does not invalidate connectedCalendars query cache, unlike disconnectMutation

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()`; it does not call `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` (or other invalidations) the way `disconnectMutation` does in `onSettled`. Since `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` now enriches results with `cacheUpdatedAt`, failing to invalidate/refetch could leave the UI showing stale cache status unless `onSuccess` triggers a refetch elsewhere (not shown in this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Plain Error thrown in deleteCache.handler.ts:22 instead of TRPCError, surfacing as generic 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR to the client
Cache-status query in connectedCalendars.handler.ts runs even when calendar-cache is disabled and can receive empty or undefined credentialIds

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, `credentialIds` is derived via `connectedCalendars.map(...)`, so it will be an array (possibly empty) but not `undefined`. The diff also does not show any calendar-cache enable/disable flag or conditional wiring; the handler always instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly. While an empty `credentialIds` could cause an unnecessary DB call, the finding’s claims about running “when disabled” and receiving “undefined” are not verifiable from the diff.

Credential ownership check in deleteCache handler only scopes by userId, ignoring team/organization and delegation credentials, causing legitimate team-managed credentials to fail deletion and inconsistent API surface

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteCache.handler.ts`, credential authorization is `findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`, so only credentials directly owned by the current user can delete cache. However, the new UI (`CredentialActionsDropdown`) can show the cache/delete-cache action even when `delegationCredentialId` is present (it only gates disconnect via `canDisconnect`, but `hasCache` alone enables the cache section). This creates a diff-visible mismatch where delegation/team-managed credentials (not scoped by `userId`) will be offered cache deletion in the UI but the API will throw "Credential not found or access denied".

adjudication_records.issue_text: No secondary check that the user is on the credential's team when credentials have a different userId owner; should check userId OR teamId in user's teams

adjudication.rationale: The new `deleteCache` endpoint authorizes strictly by `credential.userId = user.id` (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts` uses `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`). However, the UI now exposes cache actions for connected calendars based on `integrationType` and `cacheUpdatedAt` only (no ownership/team/delegation gating beyond disconnect) in `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx` (`hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt;`), and `connectedCalendars` can plausibly include non-user-owned credentials (e.g., delegation/team connections indicated by `delegationCredentialId` being threaded through the connected calendars list). In those cases, users who can see/use a credential but don’t own it will be offered “Delete cached data” and the server will reject it because there is no secondary team/delegation-based access check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache deletion removes cache rows for all users of shared credentials without invalidating/refreshing, potentially causing stale UI or racing in-flight checks

adjudication.rationale: The new `deleteCache` endpoint verifies ownership (`prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`) before deleting, so it won’t delete cache for other users’ credentials. The diff also doesn’t show any “shared credential” model where multiple users would legitimately share the same `credentialId`. While the client mutation doesn’t explicitly invalidate `connectedCalendars`, it does call `onSuccess?.()` and the finding’s stronger claims about cross-user deletion/racing aren’t verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateManyByCredentialId called on every getAvailability with empty update, causing write amplification and bumping updatedAt on all SelectedCalendars under the credential, possibly invalidating webhook watch bookkeeping

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional call inside `GoogleCalendarService` after availability caching: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});`. This introduces an extra `updateMany` DB operation on what appears to be a frequently-called availability path, with an empty `data` payload. Even if it ends up being a no-op, it’s still a write query / extra load; if Prisma/DB treats it as an update, it could also bump `updatedAt` for all `SelectedCalendar` rows under that credential. The broader claim about webhook watch bookkeeping invalidation isn’t directly shown, but the write amplification / side-effect risk is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirst without select fetches credential including encrypted access/refresh tokens into handler memory; should select only id

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })` in `deleteCache.handler.ts` without a `select`, so it will load the full Credential row. However, the claim that this necessarily includes encrypted access/refresh tokens is not verifiable from this diff (the Credential model/fields are not shown), and merely fetching the row into memory is not, by itself, a demonstrated security defect in the changed code.

matched_golden_ids: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same portability issue: using `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS-specific and will fail on Linux GNU sed due to the empty-string argument after `-i`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unconditional updateManyByCredentialId write on every availability check causes write amplification on the hottest read path

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, an unconditional `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` was added at the end of the availability-check flow (commented as updating `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`). This introduces a database `updateMany` write on what appears to be a high-frequency/read-heavy path (availability checks), which can cause write amplification and unnecessary load/contention even when no cache refresh occurs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateMany with empty data {} may be rejected by Prisma and only exists to bump updatedAt, which isn't even the source of the cache status shown in UI

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, data)` and calls it from `GoogleCalendarService` with an **empty** `data` object: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` (CalendarService.ts). An empty `data` for Prisma `updateMany` is likely to be rejected at runtime (or result in a no-op), so this call may throw or fail to achieve the stated goal of bumping `updatedAt` (since `@updatedAt` typically changes only on a real update). Separately, the UI cache status shown is sourced from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` via `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, not from `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, so even if it worked it wouldn’t affect the cache timestamp displayed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groupBy on calendarCache credentialId without a covering index on credentialId (or credentialId, updatedAt) can cause expensive scans

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new query `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ by: ["credentialId"], where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } }, _max: { updatedAt: true } })` in `packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts`. That can become expensive at scale if `CalendarCache` isn’t indexed on `credentialId` (or `(credentialId, updatedAt)`). The diff does not add any such index in the Prisma schema/migration shown, but the diff also doesn’t conclusively prove no index exists elsewhere in the model/schema.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteMany on credentialId performs unbounded bulk delete including shared rows with userId null, with no rate limiting and causes thundering-herd refetch on next availability fetch

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `deleteCache.handler.ts`, which verifies the credential belongs to the authed user (`prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`) and then does `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })`. While this is a bulk delete scoped to a single credential, the finding’s claims about deleting “shared rows with userId null” affecting others and causing “thundering-herd refetch” / needing rate limiting are not verifiable from the diff and rely on assumptions about cross-user sharing and downstream fetch behavior that aren’t shown. Clearing all cache rows for an owned credential is consistent with the feature intent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object causes Prisma validation error and prevents updatedAt from updating, breaking getAvailability after cache refresh

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService` the new call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` passes an empty `data` object. `updateMany` requires at least one field to update; an empty `data` is likely rejected by Prisma at runtime (or becomes a no-op), so it won’t reliably “touch” rows to bump `updatedAt` as the comment intends. This can cause the post-cache-refresh flow to throw or fail to update timestamps.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache handler bypasses CalendarCacheRepository abstraction, calling prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly and failing when calendar-cache feature is disabled

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the new `deleteCacheHandler` directly calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` instead of going through the `ICalendarCacheRepository` abstraction that exists in this diff (and has a mock implementation that explicitly logs "Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled"). This is a concrete, diff-grounded architecture/consistency concern. However, the claim that it will "fail when calendar-cache feature is disabled" is not verifiable from the diff alone (the handler would still work as long as the Prisma model/table exists).

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache returns raw Error instead of typed TRPCError, resulting in generic 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR that conflates not-found and access-denied conditions
connectedCalendars response shape changed without updating the Zod output schema in connectedCalendars.schema.ts, leaving tRPC contract docs out of sync

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the connectedCalendars response shape by adding `cacheUpdatedAt` in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` (mapping `connectedCalendars` to `enrichedConnectedCalendars` with `cacheUpdatedAt`). The referenced `connectedCalendars.schema.ts` is not modified in this diff (only the input schema import is shown in `_router.tsx`), so if that file defines/exports an output Zod schema used for contract/docs generation, it would now be out of sync. However, the diff does not show whether an output schema actually exists there, so the impact is not fully verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded en-US locale in Intl.DateTimeFormat ignores useLocale(), and cache_last_updated translation only added to en/common.json
getCacheStatusByCredentialIds runs an extra Prisma query on every connectedCalendars call even with empty credential list, adding latency to a hot settings page path

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the handler now always computes `credentialIds` and calls `cacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(credentialIds)` (which executes `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy(...)`) before returning. There is no guard for `credentialIds.length === 0`, so when a user has no connected calendars this still issues a Prisma query (likely returning `[]`), adding avoidable latency on a settings-page path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object in CalendarService.ts:1022 causes Prisma validation error, breaking Google Calendar availability checks in the hot path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in `CalendarService.ts` to “Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt…”. The new repository method directly calls `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`. Passing an empty `data: {}` is allowed by the TS type (`Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` has all-optional fields) but is typically rejected by Prisma client validation at runtime (update/updateMany requires at least one field in `data`). Even if it didn’t throw, it would not update `updatedAt`, contradicting the comment and breaking the intended behavior in a hot path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization failure in deleteCache.handler.ts:25-27 throws plain Error instead of TRPCError, resulting in 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN
matched_golden_ids: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify that an authorization/authentication failure is handled by throwing a generic Error, which tRPC converts to a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, and that it should instead throw a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code (e.g., FORBIDDEN).

adjudication_records.issue_text: SelectedCalendar.updateManyByCredentialId runs unconditionally on every getAvailability call outside the cache-miss branch, causing unbounded DB write amplification per availability check

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, after the cache-miss branch (`if (!availabilityFromCache) { ... }`), the diff adds an unconditional `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});`. This runs on every availability check regardless of whether availability was served from cache, causing a DB `updateMany` per call (and potentially updating `updatedAt` for all selected calendars under that credential via Prisma’s `@updatedAt` behavior). That is write amplification on a hot/read path introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27 lacks a guard for empty/undefined credential IDs, allowing undefined entries in the Prisma in: filter which can cause the query to fail

adjudication.rationale: In connectedCalendars.handler.ts, `credentialIds` is built via `connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId)`, and this diff does not show any path where `credentialId` can be `undefined`. Additionally, an empty array passed to Prisma `in: []` is generally valid and would just return no rows; the diff provides no evidence that Prisma would fail here. The finding asserts undefined entries without diff-grounded support.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCacheMutation lacks onSettled invalidation of viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, leaving UI showing stale cache status after deletion

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` callback; unlike `disconnectMutation`, it does not perform any TRPC cache invalidation (e.g., `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`). Since `cacheUpdatedAt` is sourced from `connectedCalendars.handler` via `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(...)`, the UI will only update if callers pass an `onSuccess` that refetches/invalidates. The diff shows `onSuccess` is optional, so relying on it makes the component easier to use incorrectly, but staleness cannot be proven as a guaranteed defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No coordination between cache deletion and Google webhook-driven cache repopulation, so deleted cache timestamps can immediately reappear

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `deleteCache` mutation that simply `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` and a cache status display based on `CalendarCache.updatedAt` via `groupBy(... _max.updatedAt)`. Nothing in the shown changes introduces or references Google webhook-driven cache repopulation or any race/coordination mechanism, so the claim that deleted cache timestamps can “immediately reappear” due to webhooks is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache mutation lacks server-side enforcement of Google-only credentials; the isGoogleCalendar restriction exists only in the UI

adjudication.rationale: The UI only surfaces the delete-cache action when `integrationType === GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TYPE` and `cacheUpdatedAt` is present (`CredentialActionsDropdown`: `const hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt;`), but the server-side `deleteCache` endpoint (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`) only checks that the credential belongs to the current user and then runs `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` with no validation of the credential’s integration type. This creates an API/UI mismatch and leaves the endpoint usable for non-Google credentials if called directly, even though the product intent appears Google-only.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for the new deleteCache mutation handler, including the authorization boundary that rejects a credentialId belonging to another user

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `deleteCache` tRPC mutation and handler (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx` and `deleteCache.handler.ts`) with nontrivial authorization logic (`prisma.credential.findFirst` scoped to `id` + `userId`, throwing on failure) and a destructive action (`prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany`). The diff does not add or modify any corresponding test files exercising this handler or the cross-user credentialId rejection path, so the review concern is specific and diff-grounded as missing coverage for newly added logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delegation credentials with userId: null cause the deleteCache handler to throw 'Credential not found or access denied' for calendars the UI displays, and no test pins this behavior

adjudication.rationale: The new UI shows a “Delete cached data” action whenever `hasCache` is true, even if the credential is a delegation credential (i.e., `canDisconnect` is false only when `delegationCredentialId` is set, but `hasCache` can still be true). In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, the delete-cache option is rendered under `{hasCache && (...)}` with no additional guard for delegation credentials, and it calls `deleteCacheMutation.mutate({ credentialId })`. However, the new `deleteCacheHandler` authorizes by `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id }})`, so any credential not owned by the user (including delegation credentials with `userId: null`) will trigger `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. This creates a verifiable mismatch: the UI can present an action that will reliably error for delegation credentials that appear in the connected calendars list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateManyByCredentialId calls Prisma updateMany with an empty data object, which will fail Prisma validation ('Argument data is missing') on every cache write

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` passes an empty `data` object. The repository implementation (`packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts`) forwards this to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`. Prisma `updateMany` requires a non-empty `data` payload (i.e., at least one field to update); an empty object will cause a client validation/runtime error rather than “touching” rows, so this would break the flow whenever this code path runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test verifies that SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is refreshed after a cache fill

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial behavior to refresh timestamps by calling `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` after a cache fill in `GoogleCalendarService` (CalendarService.ts), relying on Prisma’s `@updatedAt` on `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. The diff does not add or modify any tests to assert that `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` changes as a result of this cache-fill path, so the review concern (missing test coverage for this new behavior) is grounded in the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groupBy/_max logic has untested edge cases: empty array input (in: []), credential with only expired cache rows reporting stale updatedAt, and calendars with no cache rows silently coerced to null

adjudication.rationale: The new `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` implementation uses `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } }, _max: { updatedAt: true }})` without considering `expiresAt` (added/exists in `CalendarCache`), so it can report an `updatedAt` for credentials whose only cache entries are expired, which could mislead the new UI that displays `cacheUpdatedAt` (enriched in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`). The handler also intentionally maps missing rows to `null` via `cacheStatusMap.get(...) || null`, so the “silently coerced to null” part isn’t a defect but is an edge-case behavior worth testing/confirming. The empty-array `in: []` case likely just returns an empty result, so it’s not a verifiable bug, but it is an edge case that could merit test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of the satisfies type check in selectedCalendar.ts:260-262 is a silent loosening of type safety with no compensating test

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `SelectedCalendarRepository.findMany` from creating an `args` object with `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` to passing the same `{ where, select, orderBy }` object literal directly into `prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany(...)`. This does not verifiably “silently loosen” type safety: the Prisma client method is still typed to accept `Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs`, and an object literal passed as an argument is still type-checked against that parameter type. No runtime behavior change or missing-test issue is evidenced by this change in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: connectedCalendars.handler.ts enrichment logic is untested, including the || null fallback which could mis-coerce epoch-0 updatedAt values, and the tRPC response shape change (cacheUpdatedAt added) lacks updated snapshot tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new enrichment logic in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` that changes the returned `connectedCalendars` items by adding `cacheUpdatedAt` (see `enrichedConnectedCalendars` and the return object now using it). No corresponding tests or snapshots are shown in the diff, so it’s a concrete review concern that this new API/response shape and mapping logic aren’t covered. However, the specific claim about `|| null` mis-coercing an epoch-0 date is not supported here because a `Date` object is truthy even if it represents 1970-01-01.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New CredentialActionsDropdown component has no tests for its conditional-rendering logic, and no DisconnectIntegration tests were ported; a regression in the onboarding flow could remove the disconnect affordance entirely

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `CredentialActionsDropdown` with nontrivial conditional rendering (`canDisconnect`, `hasCache`, and an early `return null` when both are false) and replaces `DisconnectIntegration` usage in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx` with this new component. No corresponding test additions/updates are present in the diff to validate the new conditions or to preserve prior disconnect-visibility expectations (especially given the new `disableConnectionModification` gating inside `CredentialActionsDropdown`, which can change when the disconnect action appears). This is a concrete, diff-grounded coverage/guardrail concern rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The migration adding CalendarCache.updatedAt has no rollback/verification test (e.g., shadow-DB check with seeded rows) to confirm backfill and that schema.prisma matches the SQL, risking silent schema/SQL drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the migration SQL adds `CalendarCache.updatedAt TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` and `schema.prisma` adds `updatedAt DateTime @default(now()) @updatedAt`, which are aligned for column existence/default; there’s no evidence in the diff of a schema/SQL mismatch or “silent drift”. The complaint about missing rollback/verification/shadow-DB tests is not grounded in any added/changed test harness in this PR and is largely generic/speculative rather than a specific, verifiable issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhook.sh is a manual dev script named like a test; the webhook-invalidation path has no automated CI coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a manual script `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` (plural), not `scripts/test-gcal-webhook.sh` as stated. While the script is clearly a developer utility (starts `tmole`, edits `.env`), the claim that a specific “webhook-invalidation path has no automated CI coverage” is not something the diff can verify (no referenced invalidation codepath or test/CI configuration changes are shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:1023 updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) passes an empty data object, making Prisma updateMany a no-op so updatedAt is never bumped — dead code that silently fails the cache staleness intent
matched_golden_ids: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: calling updateManyByCredentialId with an empty data object results in no effective update, so Prisma does not bump the @updatedAt timestamp, undermining cache staleness/refresh tracking. This aligns with the golden comment’s issue and implied fix (update updatedAt explicitly).

adjudication_records.issue_text: connectedCalendars.handler.ts:5,27 instantiates new CalendarCacheRepository() directly, bypassing the repository abstraction/factory that selects the mock when calendar-cache is disabled

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` now imports the concrete `CalendarCacheRepository` and instantiates it directly (`const cacheRepository = new CalendarCacheRepository();`) to call `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`. The same diff also maintains a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` whose methods log “Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled”, implying there is (elsewhere) a disabled mode intended to swap in the mock. By directly constructing the real repository here, this code can’t participate in such swapping/DI, making it an architecture/configuration concern grounded in this change. However, the diff does not show the supposed factory/abstraction mechanism, so the “bypassing factory” part can’t be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler.ts:26 calls prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly, bypassing ICalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential and duplicating logic

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the handler deletes rows via `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` instead of routing through the calendar-cache abstraction (`ICalendarCacheRepository` / its existing `deleteManyByCredential()` method). This is a concrete architectural consistency/duplication issue introduced by the diff (repository pattern exists and is used elsewhere, e.g., `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()`), but it does not by itself demonstrate incorrect behavior or a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:97 hardcodes Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US") ignoring the app locale from useLocale()
matched_golden_ids: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue explicitly points out that Intl.DateTimeFormat is hardcoded to "en-US" and ignores the app/user locale from useLocale, which is the same locale-related date formatting problem described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:72-85 'Cache Status' row is a non-interactive DropdownMenuItem containing plain divs, causing a11y/semantics problems

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, the “Cache Status” display is rendered inside a `<DropdownMenuItem>` (which is typically an interactive/focusable menu option) but contains only static `<div>` content and no click/select handler. This can create accessibility/semantics issues (a non-actionable item presented as an actionable menuitem) and is directly evidenced by the diff at the block rendering `{hasCache && (...)}` where `<DropdownMenuItem>` wraps the status text.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:72-85 hardcodes Tailwind colors (text-gray-900, text-gray-500, dark:text-white) instead of design tokens (text-default, text-subtle), with dark:text-white being the wrong muted color

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show hardcoded Tailwind classes in `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx` (e.g., `text-gray-900`, `text-gray-500`, `dark:text-white`) within the cache status UI, but the claim that this is "wrong" or must use design tokens (e.g., `text-default`, `text-subtle`) is a design/style preference that cannot be verified as a defect or required standard from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx nested DropdownItem inside DropdownMenuItem duplicates existing dropdown-item styling

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `DropdownItem` components nested inside `DropdownMenuItem` in `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, but the claim that this “duplicates existing dropdown-item styling” is not verifiable from the diff because the styling/behavior of `DropdownItem` vs `DropdownMenuItem` is defined in `@calcom/ui/components/dropdown` and not shown here. From the diff alone, it’s not demonstrably a defect or even a concrete issue beyond a subjective styling concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler.ts:22 throws plain Error instead of TRPCError with proper codes, surfacing as opaque INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the new handler throws a plain `Error` when the credential is not found or not owned by the user (`if (!credential) { throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied"); }`). In tRPC this will be treated as an unhandled error and surfaced to clients as a generic `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` rather than an appropriate code like `NOT_FOUND` or `UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN`, making the error classification incorrect and likely opaque to consumers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:70-79 and :123-132 contain near-identical copy-paste of CredentialActionsDropdown blocks instead of an extracted render function/component

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show two very similar `actions` blocks in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx` that both render `CredentialActionsDropdown`, but this is a maintainability/style refactor suggestion (duplication) rather than a concrete defect or a clearly important non-bug issue grounded in behavior or correctness. Nothing in the diff indicates this duplication causes problems.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhook.sh is unrelated local-dev convenience tooling (hardcoded /tmp/tmole.log, relative ../.env, BSD sed -i '') bundled into a user-facing feature PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new executable dev script `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` that is unrelated to the main feature changes (calendar cache UI/handlers). The script contains local-environment assumptions (hardcoded `/tmp/tmole.log`, relative `../.env`, and `sed -i ''` which is BSD/macOS-specific), so bundling it into this feature PR is a legitimate scope/portability concern. The finding slightly misnames the file (`test-gcal-webhook.sh` vs `test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), but the substance matches what was added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dev:cron change in apps/web/package.json:11 is unrelated developer tooling in a user-facing feature PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `apps/web/package.json` script `dev:cron` from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, which is purely local developer tooling and not related to the user-facing calendar cache feature changes shown elsewhere in the PR. adjudication_records.issue_text: user.ts:899 adds googleChannelId/updatedAt to the global user select, leaking Google-specific columns into the generic UserWithCalendars type consumed by all calendars

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` to the `selectedCalendars` select in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts` (around line 899) and correspondingly widens the generic `UserWithCalendars` type in `packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts` to include those fields. That does introduce Google-specific data (`googleChannelId`) into a generally-named calendar selection/type, which is a scope/architecture concern (extra coupling/over-fetching) rather than a verifiable functional bug from this diff alone. The claim that it’s “consumed by all calendars” isn’t directly shown in the diff, so impact can’t be fully verified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _router.tsx:28 uses inline z.object({ credentialId: z.number() }) instead of a colocated deleteCache.schema.ts, breaking the established schema-file convention and preventing codegen reuse

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx`, the new `deleteCache` procedure defines its input schema inline via `.input(z.object({ credentialId: z.number() }))`, while other procedures in the same router use colocated schema modules (e.g., `ZConnectedCalendarsInputSchema` from `connectedCalendars.schema` and `ZSetDestinationCalendarInputSchema` from `setDestinationCalendar.schema`). The diff does not add a `deleteCache.schema.ts`, so the finding about breaking the established schema-file convention / reuse is diff-grounded, but it's a consistency/architecture concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) passes an empty data object which throws at runtime in Prisma updateMany, breaking Google Calendar availability lookups; also empty update wouldn't bump updatedAt

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object into `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })` (added in `packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts`). Prisma `updateMany` requires a non-empty update payload; an empty `data: {}` is a client validation/runtime error and would break the surrounding flow. Even if it didn’t throw, an empty update would not achieve the stated goal of bumping `updatedAt`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete cache-status action shown for delegation credentials but handler looks up credential by userId, so mutation always fails for delegation/team-owned credentials

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `hasCache` is independent of `canDisconnect` (`hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`), so for a delegation credential (`delegationCredentialId` truthy) the dropdown still renders and includes the “Delete cached data” action. However, the new `deleteCache` mutation handler (`deleteCache.handler.ts`) authorizes by `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`, which will reject credentials not owned by the current user (a likely case for delegation/team-owned credentials, as also implied by the existing UI logic that prevents disconnecting when `delegationCredentialId` is set). This makes the shown action fail with “Credential not found or access denied” in that scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache mutation doesn't invalidate connectedCalendars tRPC query, leaving stale cacheUpdatedAt in UI

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()`; unlike `disconnectMutation`, it does not invalidate any tRPC queries (e.g. `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`). Since `cacheUpdatedAt` is sourced from `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` (via `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), deleting cache without explicit invalidation risks the UI continuing to show the old `cacheUpdatedAt` until some external refetch occurs. The diff doesn’t show what `onSuccess` does, so staleness isn’t provably guaranteed, but the mutation itself lacks the invalidation present in the analogous disconnect flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMany change drops the satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs type-check, weakening type safety

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `const args = { ... } satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs;`, but the replacement still passes an object literal directly into `prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany({ where, select, orderBy })`, which is itself type-checked against Prisma’s `findMany` argument type. So the claim that type safety is weakened is not verifiably true from the diff (the Prisma call still enforces the same shape at compile time).
